plain.text: The high priest asked Stephen if the charges were true. Stephen answered by telling Israel's story. God appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia and told him to go to a land he would show him. God promised the land to him and his descendants, though he had no child yet. God said his descendants would be strangers in a foreign land and mistreated for four hundred years, but God would punish that nation and they would come out and worship him. God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Isaac, Jacob and the twelve patriarchs were born.

The patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him and rescued him. He gave Joseph wisdom and favour before Pharaoh, who made him ruler over Egypt. When famine came, Jacob sent his sons to Egypt to buy grain. On their second visit Joseph made himself known. Jacob and the whole family came down to Egypt, where they died, and they were buried in Shechem.

As the time drew near for God's promise to Abraham, the people grew in Egypt. A new king who did not know about Joseph oppressed them and forced them to abandon their newborn babies. Moses was born then, a beautiful child. When he was placed outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him and raised him as her own son. Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.

When Moses was forty, he visited his fellow Israelites. He saw one being mistreated and defended him, killing the Egyptian. He thought his people would realise God was using him to rescue them, but they did not. The next day he tried to make peace between two Israelites, but one pushed him aside: "Who made you ruler and judge over us?" Moses fled to Midian.

After forty years, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai. The Lord said, "I am the God of your fathers." He told Moses to take off his sandals, because the place was holy ground. God had seen his people's oppression and was sending Moses to rescue them. This same Moses, whom they had rejected, was sent as ruler and deliverer. He led them out with wonders and signs, and he said God would raise up a prophet like him. He received living words to pass on to them.

But our ancestors refused to obey Moses. In their hearts they turned back to Egypt. They told Aaron to make them gods and made an idol in the form of a calf. So God turned away and gave them over to worshipping the stars, as the prophets wrote.

Our ancestors had the tabernacle with them in the desert, made as God directed Moses. Joshua brought it into the land, and it remained until the time of David, who asked to build a dwelling place for God. But it was Solomon who built a house for him. However, the Most High does not live in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says, "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me?"

Stephen then spoke directly: "You stiff-necked people! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just like your ancestors. Was there ever a prophet your ancestors did not persecute? They killed those who predicted the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him. You received the law but have not obeyed it."

They were furious and gnashed their teeth at him. But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked up to heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. "Look, I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God." They covered their ears, rushed at him, dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul. While they stoned him, Stephen prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit." Then he fell on his knees and cried out, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." When he had said this, he fell asleep.

summary.bigIdea: Stephen retells Israel's history to show how God's people have often resisted his messengers, and dies forgiving his killers.
points: Stephen tells the story of Abraham, Joseph and Moses: God was at work even outside the land and the temple.
He says God does not live in houses made by human hands.
As he is stoned, Stephen sees Jesus and prays, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them."
summary.reflection: Stephen forgave the people who were killing him, as Jesus did. Is there someone you find hard to forgive?
